Commissioning as tested here needs ToF-labelled recordings of a training session and a normal session, about 11.6\,min in total, with the detector fitted and calibrated on about 40 normal cycles of the latter; installing and aligning the sensors and a new person at a new station were not part of this. % 11.6, 20+20 [S] faz_a4/04_unseen_sessions.md (section 6)

\emph{Commissioning:} the 51 normal cycles were reassigned 50 times to 11 test, 20 calibration and 20 pool cycles, and the detector was fitted on the opening $n\in\{5,10,15,20\}$ pool cycles; B2 and B1 were retrained in each S1 fold on $k\in\{1,2,5,10,20\}$ labelled cycles per session (10 repetitions); recording time uses one timestamp-based definition, under which the cycles of a session sum to its wall-clock time. % 51, 50, 11, 20, 20, 10 [S] faz_a2/04_commissioning.md

\emph{Recording time.} Measured as windows divided by 600 (0.1\,s frames), a pooled S1 fold model was trained on about 21.7\,min of labelled frames and a leave-one-session-out model on about 22.6\,min; estimator (ii) used s01 (about 7.8\,min) and s02 (about 3.8\,min), 10.8\,min for the fold models and 11.6\,min for the model that predicts s03--s06. % 21.7, 22.6, 7.8, 3.8, 10.8, 11.6 [S] faz_a4/04_unseen_sessions.md (section 6)

The anomaly detector additionally fits on about 20 and calibrates on about 20 normal cycles of s02 (about 1.7\,min each), which lie within the s02 recording. % 20.0, 1.67 [S] faz_a4/04_unseen_sessions.md (section 6)

\emph{Commissioning.} In recording time, about 30 normal cycles (10 for the parameters and 20 for calibration) take about 2.7\,min at the mean cycle duration of 5.4\,s, or 2.5\,min at the median of 5.0\,s. % 30, 2.7, 5.4, 2.5, 5.0 [S] paper_prep/05_gaps.md (gap 1a)
